description.narrative:
ProDEL is a Mozambican government programme that aims to strengthen the productive base and competitiveness of local micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Gaza, Inhambane and Sofala provinces with a particular focus on the enhancement of specific agricultural value chains. In a broader sense, ProDEL intend to provide support for Local Economic Development (LED) and thus contributing to poverty reduction by generating income and employment opportunities in rural areas in the three provinces.
The basic design of the programme is based on three components:
1) The strengthening of capacities in order to improve the public services for the promotion of Local Economic Development 2) Investments for the improvement of local economic infrastructure 3) The promotion of Value Chains to the benefit of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.

ProDEL är ett program med Mozambikanska regeringen med syfte att stärka den produktiva basen och konkurrenskraften för lokala mikro-, små och medelstora företag (MSME) i Gaza-, Inhambane- och Sofalaprovinserna med särskilt fokus på att förbättra specifika värdeskedjor. I en vidare mening avser ProDEL att ge stöd till lokal ekonomisk utveckling och därmed bidra till fattigdomsminskning genom att generera inkomster och sysselsättningsmöjligheter på landsbygden i de tre provinserna.
Den grundläggande designen av programmet är baserad på tre komponenter:
1) Förstärkt kapacitet för att stärka offentliga tjänster och främja lokal ekonomisk utveckling 2) Investeringar i lokal ekonomisk infrastruktur 3) Främjande av värdekedjor till förmån för mikro-, små och medelstora företag.

ProDEL is a Mozambican government programme that aims to strengthen the productive base and competitiveness of local micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Gaza, Inhambane and Sofala provinces with a particular focus on the enhancement of specific agricultural value chains. In a broader sense, ProDEL intend to provide support for Local Economic Development (LED) and thus contributing to poverty reduction by generating income and employment opportunities in rural areas in the three provinces.
The basic design of the programme is based on three components:
1) The strengthening of capacities in order to improve the public services for the promotion of Local Economic Development 2) Investments for the improvement of local economic infrastructure 3) The promotion of Value Chains to the benefit of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises.

- 75% of the involved farmers reported an increased income. While this result cannot be enlarged to the wider group of beneficiaries, it is likely that the improved local economic dynamic has benefited a larger group rather than just the involved farmers, likewise those engaged in market activities or those who have benefited from other activities, such as easier mobility thanks to the rehabilitated/constructed roads.
- there was a positive impact on strengthened capacity and awareness among central and local authorities regarding the importance of LED approaches and their mainstreaming in local planning processes.
- promotion of economic development in the rural areas of Gaza, Inhambane and Sofala Provinces, by strengthening the productive base and the competitiveness of local micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs).
- construction of relevant infrastructure, mobilising public investment which have potential (eventually not yet fully achieved in all cases) for promoting local development. Also local value-chains for MSMEs have been promoted, some already delivering benefits to local populations (such as honey and gergelim), while other yet not performing as expected (cassava and cashew).
- 1.041 temporary jobs (construction of infrastructures) and 2.643 self-employment created, while the support to value-chains would have created more than 10.000 permanent auto-employment. No sex-disaggregation is available, however it is likely that jobs sustained through markets preferentially have benefited women rather than men, as it was observed during the field mission.
- increased productivity of 15% for gergelim and 40% for cashew nut, as well as 42% for rice and an increased production of honey with the adoption of improved hives.
- 79 training sessions for local authorities (40 defined as minimum target) involving 2.483 people. The effect was never evaluated, however there was a general appreciation that this component was relevant and has helped strengthening the capacity of staff at local level).
- More than 73 initiatives have been recorded promoting LED with the support of ProDEL. These include successful initiative like the rádios comunitárias which have played an important role in the dissemination of relevant information on LED or regarding market information.
- Several studies, documents, manuals have been produced or adopted when already available, being still used by local staff, even if often on a punctual manner, especially when the supported LED libraries have limited access for non- public servants.
- A total of 42 infrastructures were completed, out of which: 19 markets, 13 roads, 4 tanks, 3 slaughterhouses, 2 veterinary pharmacies and 1 small bridge. The quality of the infrastructures built is considered remarkable, having respected standards that ensure their climate-proofness. In Sofala some of the constructed facilities where the few that have resisted to the Idai cyclone.
CROSS CUTTING ISSUES
Despite not having drafted specific strategies for addressing cross cutting issues, the programme has contributed through its activities and the achieved results to improve the conditions of women, to strengthen local governance processes and to reduce the effect of climate change by promoting adaptation measures.
ProDEL has made an effort to engage women and positively discriminate them in its activities, namely to promote women empowerment and providing opportunities for job creation and income generating activities. Overall, the programme has promoted non-discrimination and equal access, targeting vulnerable groups in rural areas, with some focus on women groups and youth, in order to facilitate their access to local economic opportunities and jobs creation. Doing so, it has contributed to the application of human rights for its target groups and beneficiaries.
While some value-chains have mainstreamed environmental aspects in their implementation, the same concerns were not found for all value-chains. A positive effect was mentioned regarding the honey value-chain development, as a deterrent against forest fires for the traditional slash-and-burn agriculture that has negative impact on the environment and biodiversity. Also, the introduction of drought resistant varieties of cassava in a semi-arid region like south of Gaza, as a measure to increase adaptation to climate change.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
